corpus.caveat: overlapping crops of three figures, two of the three scales interpolated; a maximum statistic tolerates correlated observations, a rate would not

metric.definition: criterion_topk.rank_margin, unchanged: the position of the RPN proposal that produced each surviving detection, in the RPN's own score order
metric.ceiling_note: rpn_post_nms_top_n bounds both the ranks and any K read off them; a tail at the ceiling means no cut is safe, not that K is large

estimate.rule: max(contributing proposal position) + 1, as criterion_topk.rank_margin defines safe_k
estimate.attribution_caveat: 1 of 912 attributions were ambiguous — the detection's score matched more than one proposal, and the earliest was credited. None of them is the maximum, so K rests on an unambiguous position; the ambiguity affects positions inside the distribution, not its edge.
estimate.reasoning: 912 detections over 162 tile x model runs. The 99th percentile of contributing ranks is 953 and the second largest is 982, against a maximum of 988. 722 was not the tail's edge: 51 detection(s) in the widened set came from rank 723 or beyond, so K = 723 would drop them. Applying criterion 2's own rule to the widened set gives K = 989, which is within 11 of the 1000-proposal ceiling — the honest reading is that no cut meaningfully below rpn_post_nms_top_n is safe on this corpus. Restricted to the 157 detections above the 0.5 vectorisation cut — the ones a user is ever shown — the max rank is 948 and the rule gives K = 949, with 5 of them at or beyond 723. 1 of 912 attributions were ambiguous — the detection's score matched more than one proposal, and the earliest was credited. None of them is the maximum, so K rests on an unambiguous position; the ambiguity affects positions inside the distribution, not its edge.
